title: Recent advances in opinion propagation dynamics: A 2020 Survey

key_points.claim: Survey scope: opinion dynamics models; at least 50 new papers in Q1 2020 alone, showing rapid field growth.
key_points.evidence_quote: In the first quarter of 2020, at least 50 research papers have emerged

key_points.claim: Generic opinion-dynamics ABM structure: agents on a network with initial opinions, local update rules, and a termination criterion such as steady state.
key_points.evidence_quote: Agents start with an initial opinion. Connected agents interact and update their opinion by a given clear update rule.

key_points.claim: Possible end states are consensus, polarization (two clusters) or fragmentation (more than two clusters).
key_points.evidence_quote: The convergence state may be consensus, polarization, or fragmentation.

key_points.claim: Terminology is inconsistent across the literature, e.g. for non-changing agents (leader, media, stubborn, inflexible).
key_points.evidence_quote: there is no convergence on terminology in the literature.

key_points.claim: DeGroot model is linear iterative averaging; consensus iff some power of W has a strictly positive column (Berger).
key_points.evidence_quote: The DeGroot model is an iterative averaging model.

key_points.claim: Friedkin-Johnsen extends DeGroot with stubborn agents via a susceptibility matrix D.
key_points.evidence_quote: In the FJ model, the idea of stubborn-agents is added to the DeGroot model

key_points.claim: Bounded confidence models (Deffuant-Weisbuch pairwise, Hegselmann-Krause synchronous): agents ignore opinions too distant. Confidence radius determines cluster count, with a critical value of about 0.5 and about 1/(2r) clusters.
key_points.evidence_quote: Fortunato [28] claims r = 0.5 is the critical confidence radius above which the agents come to a consensus. Moreover, the number of clusters at equilibrium is approximately 1/2r [29].

key_points.claim: Heterogeneous confidence radii (Lorenz) help consensus be reached.
key_points.evidence_quote: heterogeneity of confidence radius helps consensus to be reached

key_points.claim: Variants include edge-specific confidence radii (Shang), asymmetric DW, and opinion-difference-dependent learning rates.
key_points.evidence_quote: confidence radiuses are assigned to edges, as opposed to agents.

key_points.claim: Discrete/binary opinion models (Ising-like, Galam, Sznajd, voter) have real-world application, e.g. used to explain Trump's 2016 victory. The survey's extension topics include stubborn/biased agents, opinion manipulation, power evolution, repulsion, noise, interrelated topics, and expressed vs. private opinions.
key_points.evidence_quote: At least two studies used binary opinion models to explain Trump's 2016 victory [36, 37].

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched, but I read only roughly the first 14,000 characters (intro, preliminaries, DeGroot/FJ/bounded-confidence models, start of discrete models). I did not read the extensions sections 4-7. This is a short arXiv survey by a single author, with no peer-review status stated. It covers opinion dynamics only, a narrow slice of artificial societies, and it is mostly mathematical and network-based rather than a broader ABM treatment.
